title: STUDY TOPIC Spiritual formation [the process of becoming like Jesus] part 7
devotional:
If I were to ask you the question, what does it mean to become like Jesus, to really reflect the image of God, what would you say?

I reckon that most people would answer that question by talking about the Fruit of the Spirit, or talk about Jesus’ love, compassion and sacrifice.

Rick Warren wrote ‘Becoming like Christ does not mean losing your personality or becoming a mindless clone. God created your uniqueness, so He certainly doesn’t want to destroy it. Christ likeness is all about transforming your character, not your personality. God wants you to develop the kind of character described in the beatitudes of Jesus (Matthew 5:1-12), the fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22-23), Paul’s great chapter on love (1 Corinthians 13), and Peter’s list of the characteristics of an effective and productive life (2 Peter 1:5-8).’ The Purpose Driven Life (Zondervan, 2002) pp. 171-173.

Rick Warren is absolutely correct, however, I think that this is an incomplete or an insufficient understanding of what it means to be like Jesus. Sometimes we think that to become like Jesus is all about behaviour modification. Now, when we become Christians there should be a radical change in how we behave. However, I know some people who would not claim to be followers of Jesus, yet they are kind, loving and compassionate. (Sometimes their behaviour and way of life is better than some Christians.)

So to be like Jesus is much more than a transformation of our behaviour or lifestyle. Jesus behaved and lived the way he did because of his ‘attitude’ or the condition of his heart.

The essence of Jesus’ life was cruciformity.(Cross-Shaped)

Cruciformity is having a life that is continually being shaped by the attitudes that enabled Jesus to go to the cross. Or to put it an other way, becoming more like Jesus demands that our lives are shaped by the cross we are called to carry, just as much as Jesus’ life was shaped by the cross he had to carry.

When Jesus tells us to take up our cross and follow him, he is asking us to think like him, he is inviting us to adopt his world-view. You can see why being like Jesus is much more that having a change in behaviour, even if that change is radical.

Michael J. Gorman, in his book Cruciformity said: - “Faith is an inauguration into a community and into a life of dying, or cruciformity.”
prayer: Father may the essence of my being be reshaped by holiness.
